frontier.hypothesis: F1 — the remaining question is DISPOSITION, not grinding, and session 4 removes the last 'maybe the search was just unlucky' objection to it.
frontier.mechanism: The jtbl-infra and GTE-leaf carve-outs are gated on 'no C input to the same compiler can produce the target bytes, by construction'. This function has (A) a frame that is byte-exactly cc1's LEAF frame despite containing a jalr, with the outgoing-arg block unconditional per calls.c:1246-1252 + mips.h:1822/1830 + mips.c:4464/4474 (corpus 1/1437); (C) an 'ori $t0,$zero,1' that GNU as cannot produce from 'li 1' (corpus 3/3 small-immediate instances hand-written); (D) a contiguous length-3 ascending prologue save run that cc1 emits descending and the scheduler only reverses under an anti-dependence this function's block structure cannot supply (corpus 1/1437). Against that, scan_hand_coded.py returns tier=LOW 0/8 — but it has no frame-geometry signal, no assembler-macro signal and no prologue-order signal, i.e. it is blind to all three. Session 4 adds that a 107k-iteration unbiased search from two chassis never beat the floor, so the hand-enumeration was not merely unlucky.
